I am 57, farming 2.6 mu of chili in Quzhou. I never went to school. I do what my mother did and what my neighbors do. Forty years in the dirt teaches you more than any book.

For chili, I start after the frost is gone, usually late April. I buy seedlings from the market in town — the red long type, same as what Old Wang grows next to me. His chili always sells well, so I follow him. I do not know the variety name, just "the red long one." It is better than the old seeds my mother used — bigger peppers, more on each plant.

Before planting, I spread manure from my neighbor's pig pen — maybe 3 carts on my 2.6 mu, whatever he gives me cheap. Then I hire the tractor man to come plough and rotary the field, 40 yuan per mu, he comes one morning. Then I make the ridges myself with a hoe.

For fertilizer, I use the compound bag, the 15-15-15 one, two bags on my whole field before planting. That is 100 jin, about 50 kg, so maybe 20 kg per mu. Then when the plants start flowering I put urea, one bag (50 jin) for the whole field, maybe 10 kg per mu. When the peppers are swelling I put another half bag urea and some potassium — the red bag, one bag for the field. Too little fertilizer and the peppers are small, nobody buys small peppers. I would rather spend an extra 50 yuan on fertilizer than lose 200 yuan of peppers.

Water — I have the well. I water after transplanting, then every 10 days or so when it is dry, more when peppers are filling. Maybe 8 or 9 times in the season.

Pests — chili gets aphids and the rot disease. I spray when I see bugs or spots. Usually 5 or 6 times through the season. I buy from the agri-shop in town, whatever the shopkeeper gives me for chili. If neighbors are spraying, I spray too.

Last year I got about 1800 jin of dry-weight equivalent per mu, fresh maybe 2500 kg. I hope for the same this year.
